chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Abdullah ibn Sinan who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Charity given with the hand protects from an evil death, repels seventy types of afflictions, and finds its way through the beards of seventy devils — all of them commanding him not to do it.'

key_terms.الصَّدَقَةُ بِالْيَدِ: Charity given directly with one's own hand — emphasizing the personal, immediate act of giving
key_terms.الْبَلَاء: Afflictions, tribulations, trials — any form of divine test or worldly calamity
key_terms.لُحِيِّ شَيْطَاناً: Beards of devils — an idiomatic expression meaning the charity overcomes or passes through the grip of satanic forces
key_terms.مِيتَةَ السَّوْءِ: An evil or bad death — dying in a state of sin, disgrace, or spiritual deprivation

ai.seo_question: What does Islam say about the benefits of giving charity with one's own hand?
ai.summary: Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) emphasizes the extraordinary spiritual power of giving charity with one's own hand. The hadith presents sadaqa as a triple-layered protection: it guards against a bad death, wards off seventy categories of misfortune, and overcomes the collective resistance of seventy satanic forces who urge one to withhold it. The vivid imagery of charity 'passing through the beards of seventy devils' illustrates how the act of giving transcends even organized demonic opposition.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Abdullah Bin Sinan who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘The charity with the hand negates the evil death and repels seventy types from the types of the afflictions, and it (charity) finds its way through the beards of seventy devils, all of them instructing him that he should not do so’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan who has said the following: “

I heard abu ‘ Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, say, ‘Giving charity by one’s own hand repels seventy kinds of misfortune, which finds its way out through the beards of seven hundred Satans who all try to stop him from giving charity.’”
